Description: ticket.ausecurity.best is an osTicket v1.18.4 instance that has not been installed. Unauthenticated GET requests to /setup/install.php and /setup/ return HTTP 200 and the osTicket prerequisites wizard (PHP/MySQL checks passing, continue form present, PHPSESSID cookie set). Application paths including /scp/login.php, /login.php, /kb/, and /api/http.php all HTTP 302 to /setup/install.php, confirming the product is in pre-install state rather than a leftover file on a live helpdesk. The same installer is also served in cleartext on TCP 8080 (Apache/2.4.68, PHP/8.2.33). Completing the wizard was not performed. If completed by an attacker, they could choose the admin account and database settings and take full control of the future support platform, including customer tickets. Recommendation: Take the host offline until osTicket is installed privately. Restrict /setup/ to localhost or remove the setup directory after install. Require HTTPS only and close TCP 8080 if it is not needed. Place the helpdesk behind authentication and a firewall allowlist where possible. --- # Finding: DOM-based cross-site scripting on consultation success page Severity: medium CVSS: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N Affected: https://ausecurity.best/consultation-success.html, https://www.ausecurity.best/consultation-success.html, https://contact.ausecurity.best/consultation-success.html References: https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/DOM_Based_XSS Summary: A crafted link on the public website can run an attacker’s script in a visitor’s browser. Description: consultation-success.html reads the `name` query parameter with URLSearchParams and assigns it to the DOM with innerHTML (element id user-name). The `company` parameter is assigned with textContent and is not this sink. The contact API (POST /api/contact) returns redirect_url=/consultation-success.html?name=&company=, and main.js sets window.location.href to that value. Direct evidence: the page JavaScript contains `document.getElementById('user-name').innerHTML = userName`. A malicious URL such as /consultation-success.html?name= is sufficient proof; the payload was not driven further. Impact is session/script execution in the site origin for any user who opens the link. Recommendation: Stop using innerHTML for untrusted URL data. Use textContent (as already done for company). Encode output and add a strict Content-Security-Policy. Validate redirect_url on the client to same-origin paths without embedding raw HTML. --- # Finding: Self-signed TLS certificate and hostname mismatch on the main site Severity: medium CVSS: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N Affected: https://ausecurity.best/, https://www.ausecurity.best/, https://contact.ausecurity.best/, 51.79.166.148:443 References: Summary: The main website uses a homemade certificate that browsers do not trust, and www/contact names are not on the certificate. Description: openssl against 51.79.166.148 with server name ausecurity.best returned a certificate subject CN=ausecurity.best, issuer CN=ausecurity.best (self-signed), SAN DNS:ausecurity.best only, valid 2026-09-14 to 2027-09-14. www.ausecurity.best and contact.ausecurity.best present the same certificate, so the hostname does not match. Visitors see warnings; a network attacker can more easily intercept or replace the session because there is no public-CA chain to pin trust. blog.ausecurity.best and ticket.ausecurity.best correctly use Let’s Encrypt certificates and are not this issue. Recommendation: Issue a publicly trusted certificate (Let’s Encrypt or commercial) covering ausecurity.best, www.ausecurity.best, and contact.ausecurity.best. Enable HSTS after HTTPS works without warnings. --- # Finding: Marketing site and ticket installer served over cleartext HTTP on port 8080 Severity: medium CVSS: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N Affected: http://51.79.166.148:8080/, http://51.79.166.209:8080/, http://51.79.166.209:8080/setup/install.php References: Summary: The same websites are also available without encryption on an extra port, so traffic can be read or changed on the network. Description: nmap showed TCP 8080 open on 51.79.166.148 (nginx 1.25.5) and 51.79.166.209 (Apache 2.4.68). GET http://51.79.166.209:8080/ returned 302 to /setup/install.php and the osTicket installer over HTTP. Port 80 on the main site correctly 301s to HTTPS; port 8080 does not. This exposes page content and the installer to passive interception. Recommendation: Disable port 8080 or bind it to localhost.
